stimulus:
"Hope" is the thing with feathers -
That perches in the soul -
And sings the tune without the words -
And never stops - at all -

And sweetest - in the Gale - is heard -
And sore must be the storm -
That could abash the little Bird
That kept so many warm -

I've heard it in the chillest land -
And on the strangest Sea -
Yet - never - in Extremity,
It asked a crumb - of me.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: "Perches in the soul": retrospective lineage barcoding of primed cells
ideas.description: Barcode a clonal population with heritable lineage tags, split it, profile one half by scRNA-seq before drug exposure and sequence barcodes in survivors after, so the pre-treatment transcriptional state of surviving lineages can be reconstructed. This distinguishes a rare pre-existing primed subpopulation from a state induced by the drug itself.

ideas.title: "The tune without the words": RNA-protein mismatch in survivors
ideas.description: Jointly measure single-cell transcript and protein levels for the drug target and bypass pathways using CITE-seq or smFISH combined with immunofluorescence. This tests whether survivors are defined by translational or post-translational buffering that is invisible to transcript-only resistance screens.

ideas.title: "Never stops at all": continuous live-cell tracking of survival trajectories
ideas.description: Perform long-term time-lapse imaging with signaling and cell-cycle reporters spanning drug addition, tracking each cell's complete history. This reveals whether survival reflects a persistent fluctuating state, cell-cycle phase at the moment of exposure, or stochastic escape from apoptotic commitment.

ideas.title: "Sweetest in the Gale": dense sampling of transient states during treatment
ideas.description: Profile cells at many time points during the first 72 hours of treatment rather than only before and after, since the decisive state may be transient. Pair this with drug-on/drug-off pulse schedules to test whether the surviving state is reversible and the cells re-sensitizable.

ideas.title: "Never asked a crumb": single-cell metabolic frugality of persisters
ideas.description: Quantify per-cell biosynthetic and metabolic demand in survivors using SCENITH or puromycin-incorporation translation-rate assays alongside dormancy markers and nutrient-limitation challenges. This tests whether persistence is an actively maintained low-consumption quiescent program rather than specific signaling rewiring.
